aliases: Get started with AGI Code (VS Code walkthrough)
feature.summary: Short first-run flows on each app. Web has a two-step wizard at /welcome with starter prompts. Mobile has hero, about-you and device-setup screens. The CLI has a terminal setup wizard. VS Code has a walkthrough and a first-run panel. Chrome opens a Welcome page on install. Each can be skipped.

purpose.what_it_does: Greets a first-time person, asks for light personalization or setup, and then lands them in the first chat. Web asks for a preferred name and work description, then offers starter prompts. Mobile asks to accept terms, collects name and work, then offers a local model download or sign in to Cloud. (apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx:36) (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:280)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says first-time users are shown a short introduction to key features before or at their first chat (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/012-new-chat-experience.md, S12.22). Mobile requirements: onboarding shows brand and privacy summary, explains Local, BYOK and Cloud, checks local model readiness and never blocks Local use (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, M-ONB-001 to M-ONB-005).
problems_solved: Empty new-chat screens do not tell a new person what to do.
Personal details (name, work) make the first replies fit the person.
Setup of how to connect (account, own key, local model) must happen once.
use_cases: After sign-up on web, answer 'What should we call you?' and pick a starter prompt that fills the composer.
Install the mobile app, tap 'Start chatting', accept the notice, download the recommended local model, and land in chat.
Run the CLI for the first time and choose how to connect.
Install the Chrome extension and read the Welcome page.

established.statement: First-time users are shown a short introduction to key features before or at their first chat.
Complete and skip persist across reload; delayed profile loading never overwrites an edited field; read and save failures expose a recoverable state without claiming completion.

Mobile onboarding shows brand, Local-first positioning and a privacy summary, lets the user proceed without an account, explains Local, BYOK and Cloud, checks local model readiness, and does not block Local use with sign-in.
No language, time zone or memory step at sign-up.

acceptance_criteria: A new signed-in web user without the completed marker sees the two-step wizard at /welcome; a user with it is sent to /chat.
'Skip for now' lands in /chat and /welcome then redirects to /chat on later visits.
Choosing a starter prompt lands in /chat with that prompt in the composer and removes the query parameter.
A save failure shows an error and lets the person retry.
Mobile first launch shows the hero, and after finishing, relaunch goes straight to the app.
CLI first run shows the connection menu once; re-run needs 'agi onboarding'.
Chrome install opens the Welcome page once.

Failure of the seed read lets the wizard still show with an account name fallback [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Make the trigger for /welcome explicit and tested (redirect after sign-up).

steps.what_happens: The server page reads the identity, checks terms and age, and reads the completed marker from the account.
The wizard loads the saved name and work description from the 'general' preference namespace and prefills.
Finish or skip saves the namespace with onboardingCompletedAt and refreshes profile consumers, then routes to /chat.
Mobile stores the choices on the device and sets 'onboarding-done'; the disclosure acceptance goes to a device ledger.
Mobile local model download pulls the recommended model from its host, with checksum.
CLI wizard writes .setup_complete in the config folder.
VS Code stores the seen flag in extension global state.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Web wizard uses no model. Mobile recommends a local model by device tier and activates it on finish (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:252). corrections.claim: CLI wizard runs once per config folder and writes a marker file; Ctrl+C writes no marker
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The marker .setup_complete is written at Step 8 (onboarding.rs:1007) after every path that reaches the end. That includes 'Skip for now' / AuthChoice::Skip, which only prints 'Skipped authentication' (:887-893). So choosing Skip does mark setup complete and the wizard never shows again. Cancelling at the auth menu returns Ok(false) with no marker (:814-821). The 'Setup interrupted' text at :808 belongs to the trust-folder step, not Ctrl+C in general.
corrections.correction: The CLI writes .setup_complete when the flow reaches the end, including after 'Skip for now'. Cancelling at the folder-trust or connection-menu step writes no marker, so the wizard returns on the next run.

corrections.claim: Mobile local model download pulls the recommended model from its host, with checksum (onboarding.tsx:346-362)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: There are two paths. The ExecuTorch preset path calls prepareModel(presetModel) with no checksum condition. The checksum is required only on the second path (downloadUrl && checksum && format, :365-372). Both go through useModelInstallStore.prepareModel.
corrections.correction: The recommended model downloads through the model install store. Only the non-preset path requires a catalog checksum, download URL and format. The preset path is handled by the store's own logic.

corrections.claim: Local mode: Mobile and CLI onboarding both have a Local path that needs no account ('Local model, no account needed.')
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The CLI string exists (onboarding.rs:843), on the AuthChoice::Local branch. The cited line is not Mobile evidence, and I did not open a mobile string for the claim. Mobile has 'Continue without downloading' and 'Sign in to use Cloud'. Mobile also makes the age gate come first, and that gate uses FEATURES.auth and the account age confirmation, so it can depend on the account.
corrections.correction: CLI Local path needs no account (onboarding.rs:841). For Mobile, the age gate runs before onboarding and is keyed to the account age check, so describe it as such instead of 'no account'.

corrections.what_the_code_shows: The first-run wizard runs only when cli.command is none, cli.prompt is none, not dump_system_prompt, interactive::can_prompt() is true and the marker is absent (lib.rs:6112-6119). So it is skipped for any subcommand, a prompt argument or --dump-system-prompt, not only when non-interactive. The explicit 'agi onboarding' command (lib.rs:7803) runs it regardless.
corrections.correction: The wizard is skipped when a subcommand, a prompt or --dump-system-prompt is given, or when no terminal can prompt.

missing_facts: The web wizard's save-failure and skip behaviours are in apps/web/features/onboarding/components/OnboardingWizard.tsx. The page does not say that the wizard also requires terms acceptance and adult eligibility on every visit, which are enforced as redirects in apps/web/app/welcome/page.tsx:18-20, so a signed-in user who has not accepted terms cannot reach the wizard.

The CLI wizard's trust-folder step (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:800-808) can end the whole flow with no marker. The page treats 'Setup interrupted' as a Ctrl+C message, but it is the folder-trust failure message.
The CLI 'Skip for now' still writes .setup_complete (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:887-893,1007), so skipping means the first-run wizard never reappears. The page does not state this.
